[[File:Samakumine Jinja Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Torii}}]]
'''Samakumine Shrine''' (さまくみねじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}, {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|Q274384|qid=Q274384}}, {{ill|Taira Nakayama|Q128846768|qid=Q128846768}}. It is listed as a minor shrine in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} and was formerly ranked as a gōsha under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the first year of {{ill|Keiun|Q428753|qid=Q428753}} ({{ill|704|Q23503|qid=Q23503}}).

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as one of seven shrines in {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}}, {{ill|Iwaki district|Q11585428|qid=Q11585428|lt=Iwaki District}}, and was classified as a minor shrine. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it received patronage from the {{ill|Iwakitaira Domain|Q843782|qid=Q843782}}. When it was destroyed by lightning in the second year of {{ill|Tenna|Q1145289|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenna}} ({{ill|1682|Q7648|qid=Q7648}}), the shrine buildings were rebuilt the following year by the domain lord {{ill|Naitō Yoshimune|Q8514975|qid=Q8514975|lt=Naitō Yoshiyasu}}, and thereafter successive lords carried out further repairs and renovations.

In the ninth year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}}), it was officially designated as a gōsha.
